legal_basis: Local Authorities (Members' Allowances) (England) Regulations 2003, regulation 15: every council publishes, each year, the total paid to each councillor under each heading of its members' allowances scheme.

frameworks.title: Wales: every councillor's basic salary, 2026-27
frameworks.publisher: Democracy and Boundary Commission Cymru, Annual Remuneration Report 2026-27
frameworks.note: Set nationally for all 22 Welsh councils, from 1 April 2026. Senior salaries (leader, cabinet members, committee chairs) are set in bands; the leader of the largest councils gets £78,917.

frameworks.title: Scotland: every councillor's salary, 2025-26
frameworks.publisher: Scottish Government: councillors' roles, conduct and pay
frameworks.note: Set nationally for all 32 Scottish councils from 1 April 2025 (the latest rate on gov.scot). Leaders of Glasgow City and the City of Edinburgh get £71,519; Aberdeen City £60,791; Dundee City £50,063.

not_covered.name: Kent, Hampshire, Lancashire, Norfolk, Essex, Leicestershire, Derbyshire and East Sussex county councils; Manchester City Council
not_covered.reason: each publishes its statement, but its website refuses automated downloads from the servers that refresh this site, so the figures cannot be kept up to date automatically.

not_covered.name: Devon, West Sussex and Hertfordshire county councils; Liverpool City Council
not_covered.reason: no downloadable statement of the amounts paid to each councillor was found on the council's website; the statement may only be available on request.

not_covered.name: Oxfordshire County Council
not_covered.reason: publishes monthly pay reports rather than an annual statement; adding them up is planned.

not_covered.name: Worcestershire County Council
not_covered.reason: publishes the rates in its scheme, not the amounts paid to each councillor.

not_covered.name: Nottingham City Council
not_covered.reason: its latest published statement is for 2023-24 and its PDF layout cannot be read reliably.
